summary: Germany is part of the Schengen Area: EU and EFTA citizens enter freely, around 60 visa-exempt nationalities can stay 90 days in any 180-day period (the ETIAS travel authorization is not yet in operation), and everyone else needs a Schengen short-stay visa costing €90, applied for via the Federal Foreign Office's consular network.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Germany?
faq.answer: No. US passport holders can visit Germany and the rest of the Schengen Area visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Once ETIAS becomes mandatory, they will need to obtain this online authorization (€20) before travel.

faq.question: How much does a Germany Schengen visa cost?
faq.answer: The Schengen short-stay visa costs €90 for adults and €45 for children aged 6–11. A national long-stay visa (Type D) costs €75. Short-stay visas allow up to 90 days in any 180-day period across all Schengen countries.

faq.question: Is ETIAS required to enter Germany?
faq.answer: ETIAS for visa-exempt travelers is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. Once mandatory, the €20 online authorization will be required before boarding. Check the official EU website for the current status.

faq.question: How can I move to Germany for work?
faq.answer: Work in Germany needs a national (D) visa, which costs €75 under the Residence Ordinance (AufenthV § 46). No official source we could read here sets out the conditions of the EU Blue Card or the Opportunity Card.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Germany without a visa?
faq.answer: Visa-exempt non-EU visitors can stay up to 90 days within any 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area. EU and EFTA citizens do not need a visa.
